description: What a Line on security.sbom-import reads: one SBOM file in the workspace (CycloneDX JSON or SPDX 2.2/2.3 JSON, detected by content) and the source label it is recorded under; one Line per SBOM file. Each component's occurrence takes the scope the SBOM states (CycloneDX scope, or SPDX relationships; required when none is stated) and, for container distro packages with a stated release and source package, its osv_package. A scope other than required, optional or excluded is refused for that component, which keeps the scope it held; a purl listed twice with two scopes writes nothing for that purl.

logical_source.description: Source label the SBOM Capture and its derived component list are recorded under, lowercase (the template uses cyclonedx.sbom.app). Give each SBOM Line its own; evidence requirements and landing Triggers can name it.

relative_path.description: Workspace-relative path of one CycloneDX JSON SBOM (bomFormat CycloneDX; tested with spec 1.6) or SPDX 2.2/2.3 JSON SBOM (spdxVersion SPDX-2.2 or SPDX-2.3; e.g. GitHub dependency-graph export, syft -o spdx-json, trivy --format spdx-json), detected by content: at most 1 MiB and 20000 components (CycloneDX nested at most 16 levels deep). The root component's purl (CycloneDX metadata.component.purl or SPDX described package's purl) names the inventory; without one, the inventory is named by this path, so moving the file starts a new inventory. Every component needs a purl: one without is counted but not imported, and the run then retires nothing. A generator for the project's ecosystem writes the file (cyclonedx-py, syft, cdxgen, trivy); Cruxible does not.

name: security.sbom-import.params
